From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP & evaluation for hosting (EU rollout)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — great to see CloudHealth moving quickly. I attached a one-page MAP and a hosting decision matrix (MAP_v0.1.xlsx) that maps your primary criteria to a recommended path. Quick summary:

- PoC: Hosted for fast results (2–3 weeks) using EU region nodes so you can validate latency and basic integration.
- Perf validation & quantization trials: Dedicated (reserved capacity) for repeatable throughput measurements and deterministic p95 latency.
- Regulated data flows / audit scope: Private (VPC/on-prem) recommended if you need customer-controlled networking and HSM/KMS.

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
1) Week 1–2: POA & PoC environment (Hosted EU) — integration + basic prompts
2) Week 3–5: Perf runs & tooling (Dedicated if needed for throughput)
3) Week 6–7: Security evidence exchange (SOC2 artifacts, IAC snippets)
4) Week 8–10: Contract & procurement (pricing, SLA, data terms)

I've included gating criteria in the spreadsheet. Two asks from our side: a short list of compliance constraints (data residency + logging retention) and a single technical owner to coordinate perf runs.

Attaching: MAP_v0.1.xlsx, redwood-sla-draft.pdf

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: MAP_v0.1.xlsx; redwood-sla-draft.pdf

Sarah / Marcus —

Quick technical notes from infra for the MAP and to help you choose:

- Latency: If target p95 <= 120ms at your expected token rate, Hosted EU (m5-optimized nodes) should be fine for initial rollout. If sustained concurrency > 300 rps we should move to Dedicated to avoid noisy-neighbor variance.
- Data residency: Hosted EU nodes can satisfy residency, but log export to a customer-controlled S3 requires Dedicated or Private with VPC endpoints (privacy teams usually insist on the latter).
- KV cache & batching: For high throughput inference, Dedicated gives deterministic batch scheduling and better unit costs.
- Security evidence: we can provide SOC2 excerpts; for audit-level artifacts (raw logs, HSM attestation) Private deployment is the path.

I recommend this pattern for CloudHealth: start with Hosted for PoC (fast), move to Dedicated for perf/regression tests, then decide Private if procurement/compliance mandate it. This reduces ramp time while giving you measurement-backed decision points.

I'll reserve a small Dedicated pool for the week of Oct 18 if you want to run perf trials — tell me the window.

—Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
